units.title: A cult classic with modest beginnings
units.preview: After dynamic advertisements, the hosts introduce The Secret of Monkey Island, contrast its modest original sales with its lasting reputation, and discuss how limited colours shaped its atmosphere.
units.question: How do the hosts explain the gap between the game's moderate initial sales and its growing cultural reputation?

units.title: Pirate influences and adventure-game ancestors
units.preview: The discussion connects the game to Disney's Pirates of the Caribbean ride, pirate popular culture, and earlier text-heavy adventure games.
units.question: Which cultural and technical predecessors helped shape Monkey Island, and what limitations did earlier games impose on players?

units.title: Lucasfilm turns language into gameplay
units.preview: The hosts explain how point-and-click commands removed guesswork and place the project within George Lucas's wider experiments in games, graphics, and visual effects.
units.question: Why did a menu of visible commands represent a major change even though it sounds ordinary today?

units.title: Designing out dead ends and cheap deaths
units.preview: Ron Gilbert's design philosophy rejected unwinnable states and repetitive deaths, while licensing constraints pushed Lucasfilm Games toward original experimental projects and the SCUMM engine.
units.question: How did creative restrictions and Gilbert's frustrations with other games lead to more player-friendly design?

units.title: Writing a comedy the player can inhabit
units.preview: Programming and dialogue writing happened together, producing an interactive comedy whose inexperienced young hero made player mistakes feel natural.
units.question: How does Guybrush's personality turn imperfect player choices into part of the comedy rather than a failure?

units.title: From Guy to Guybrush
units.preview: The episode closes with the accidental origin of Guybrush's name, casual naming decisions elsewhere in the game, and the outro advertisements.
units.question: What do the naming stories reveal about the informal and collaborative nature of the game's development?

vocab.definition: something used or valued regularly and considered basic or essential
vocab.tip: A staple holds papers together; metaphorically, a staple holds a routine or culture together.
vocab.example: Point-and-click adventures became a staple of 1990s computer gaming.

vocab.cn: 大张旗鼓的宣传；隆重欢迎
vocab.definition: public attention, celebration, or publicity surrounding an event
vocab.tip: Originally a short ceremonial trumpet flourish; now often used in 'with little fanfare'.
vocab.example: The product arrived with little fanfare but gradually found a loyal audience.

vocab.definition: to a very great degree
vocab.tip: immense + -ly; compare enormously and tremendously.
vocab.example: The game remains immensely popular among players of a certain generation.

vocab.definition: a period associated with the production or origin of something
vocab.tip: From wine production; 'of a certain vintage' politely refers to age or generation.
vocab.example: Gamers of a similar vintage often share the same references.

vocab.definition: neither very large nor very small in amount or degree
vocab.tip: mod- relates to measure; moderation means avoiding extremes.
vocab.example: Initial demand was moderate rather than spectacular.

vocab.definition: creating a distinctive and emotionally engaging mood
vocab.tip: atmosphere + -ic; useful for films, music, games, and places.
vocab.example: Careful lighting made the limited graphics surprisingly atmospheric.

vocab.definition: having great power, influence, or effect
vocab.tip: Related to potential and omnipotent through the Latin root pot-, meaning power.
vocab.example: A theme-park attraction can become a potent source of cultural imagery.

vocab.definition: a work that continues the story or subject of an earlier one
vocab.tip: From Latin sequi, 'to follow'; sequence shares the same root.
vocab.example: The successful film produced several sequels.

vocab.definition: the circumstances that help explain the meaning of something
vocab.tip: con- (together) + text (woven): ideas woven together around a detail.
vocab.example: Without historical context, the joke sounds much older than it is.

vocab.definition: while still developing inside the uterus
vocab.tip: A Latin phrase used humorously in the episode to reject an impossible childhood experience.
vocab.example: She joked that she could not have played the game in utero.

vocab.definition: operated or presented mainly through written words rather than graphics
vocab.tip: The hyphen joins a noun and participle into one modifier.
vocab.example: Early text-based games required players to type commands.

vocab.definition: an instruction given to a computer or person
vocab.tip: In computing, command is countable: enter, select, or execute a command.
vocab.example: A visible command menu reduced the need for trial and error.

vocab.definition: communication or action involving two or more participants or systems
vocab.tip: inter- (between) + action; interactive describes a system that responds to users.
vocab.example: The interface made interaction depend on both images and language.

vocab.definition: too small or unimportant to deserve much attention
vocab.tip: in- (not) + significant; the speaker contrasts apparent insignificance with historical importance.
vocab.example: The change may look insignificant now, but it transformed the user experience.

vocab.definition: an activity that is secondary to someone's main work
vocab.tip: From the line beside a sports field; a sideline project sits outside the main activity.
vocab.example: The experimental game began as a sideline project.

vocab.definition: a business organization or an ambitious undertaking
vocab.tip: enter- + prise (undertaking); entrepreneurial belongs to the same word family.
vocab.example: The filmmaker expanded his enterprise into several technical fields.

vocab.definition: introducing methods or ideas that have not been used before
vocab.tip: A pioneer explores new territory; pioneering work opens a new field.
vocab.example: The studio invested in pioneering visual-effects technology.

vocab.definition: to change the public identity, name, or image of an organization
vocab.tip: re- (again) + brand; often used in the passive: be rebranded as.
vocab.example: The graphics division was later rebranded under a famous new name.

vocab.definition: a feeling of annoyance or something that repeatedly causes it
vocab.tip: irritate → irritated/irritating → irritation.
vocab.example: A common irritation was discovering that an earlier mistake made the game unwinnable.

vocab.definition: smooth and continuous, with no obvious breaks or difficulties
vocab.tip: seam + -less: literally without a visible join.
vocab.example: The designers wanted progression to feel seamless.

vocab.cn: 逃避责任的做法；敷衍手段
vocab.definition: an easy but unsatisfactory way of avoiding a difficult problem
vocab.tip: Informal noun; usually appears as 'an easy cop-out'.
vocab.example: Repeatedly killing the player can feel like a design cop-out.

vocab.definition: to make something last longer than it otherwise would
vocab.tip: pro- (forward) + long; prolong gameplay, conflict, or uncertainty.
vocab.example: Artificial difficulty may prolong gameplay without making it more enjoyable.

vocab.cn: 雄心勃勃的；规模宏大的
vocab.definition: requiring great effort and aiming for an impressive result
vocab.tip: ambition is the noun; ambitious can describe people or projects.
vocab.example: Licensing limits encouraged the team to attempt more ambitious original projects.

vocab.definition: a graphical representation of a user in a digital environment
vocab.tip: The computing sense comes from a Sanskrit word for a deity's earthly manifestation.
vocab.example: The experimental online world allowed users to interact through avatars.

vocab.definition: to obtain something from a particular source
vocab.tip: Common pattern: derive A from B; be derived from B.
vocab.example: Players derived pleasure from the comedy as well as the puzzles.

vocab.definition: deeply involved in an activity or fictional world
vocab.tip: immerse literally means put under liquid; metaphorically, become fully absorbed.
vocab.example: The dialogue helped young players feel immersed in the story.

vocab.definition: the main character in a story, game, or drama
vocab.tip: Contrast protagonist with antagonist, the main opposing force.
vocab.example: An inexperienced protagonist can make a player's mistakes believable.

vocab.definition: lacking experience or sophisticated judgment
vocab.tip: Pronounced /naɪˈiːv/; the two vowel sounds belong to separate syllables.
vocab.example: The hero is naive, but his enthusiasm makes him appealing.

vocab.definition: a person who is new to an activity and has little experience
vocab.tip: The adjective beginner is less formal; novice is useful for skills and professions.
vocab.example: The novice pirate learns by experimenting rather than following instructions.

vocab.cn: 普通人式角色；平凡人代表
vocab.definition: an ordinary and relatable character intended to represent typical people
vocab.tip: Written as one word when it names the literary character type.
vocab.example: The hero functions as an everyman despite the fantastic setting.

vocab.definition: a digital image represented as a grid of individual pixels
vocab.tip: bit + map: a map of binary picture information.
vocab.example: The character's bitmap file accidentally supplied his final name.

vocab.definition: not having or not being given a name
vocab.tip: name + -less; compare faceless, countless, and endless.
vocab.example: The nameless protagonist was initially called simply Guy.

vocab.cn: 系列作品中的一部；分期部分
vocab.definition: one part of a series published or released over time
vocab.tip: Also spelled instalment in British English; context distinguishes it from a payment installment.
vocab.example: A later installment turned the naming joke into a family tradition.

vocab.definition: to accept and deliberately emphasize a quality, trend, or situation
vocab.tip: Originally physical; now common in informal discussions of branding and storytelling.
vocab.example: The sequel leaned into the accidental joke instead of ignoring it.

vocab.definition: relaxed and not carefully planned or formal
vocab.tip: Casual can describe clothing, speech, decisions, or employment; context changes its meaning.
vocab.example: Some of the most memorable names emerged from casual working labels.

vocab.definition: a humorous imitation of a recognizable work, style, or scene
vocab.tip: Parody imitates for comic effect; satire uses humour to criticize.
vocab.example: The writers chose a name that enabled a parody of a famous film scene.

expressions.cn: 几乎没有宣传或庆祝地
expressions.definition: without attracting much public attention
expressions.example: The innovative title was released with little fanfare.

expressions.cn: 属于某一代的；有些年纪的
expressions.definition: a tactful or humorous way to describe people or things from a particular period
expressions.example: The reference is instantly familiar to gamers of a certain vintage.

expressions.definition: an informal way to place a number within a broad range
expressions.example: Sales were north of one hundred thousand and south of one million.

expressions.definition: to increase continuously over an extended period
expressions.example: The game's reputation continued to grow and grow.

expressions.definition: to remember an important fact while judging a situation
expressions.example: Keep in mind that many modern interface conventions did not yet exist.

expressions.definition: to lack knowledge or understanding of something
expressions.example: She had no idea the familiar song came from a theme-park ride.

expressions.definition: to exist or happen earlier than something else
expressions.example: Several text adventures came before the graphical game.

expressions.definition: to attempt an answer without enough information
expressions.example: Players often had to guess at the exact wording of a command.

expressions.definition: to control software by moving a pointer and selecting visible items
expressions.example: Point-and-click controls made the world easier to explore.

expressions.definition: to express words audibly rather than silently
expressions.example: The innovation sounds minor when you say it out loud today.

expressions.definition: to pursue unfamiliar or innovative possibilities
expressions.example: The company used its resources to push in new directions.

expressions.definition: to have a particular name or reputation
expressions.example: The division later became known as LucasArts.

expressions.text: run someone into a dead end
expressions.cn: 使某人陷入无法继续的局面
expressions.definition: to leave someone in a situation with no possible progress
expressions.example: A missing object could run the player into a dead end.

expressions.cn: 一步走错；一个错误操作
expressions.definition: a single mistake with serious consequences
expressions.example: In some older games, one wrong move meant starting again.

expressions.cn: 超越时代的；理念超前的
expressions.definition: more advanced or innovative than contemporary expectations
expressions.example: The avatar-based online community was far ahead of its time.

expressions.cn: 以类似方式；遵循相似思路
expressions.definition: using a comparable approach or design
expressions.example: The reusable engine helped the studio build several games along similar lines.

expressions.definition: to participate in an activity or event
expressions.example: The interface made players feel they were taking part in a comedy.

expressions.cn: 跌跌撞撞地进入；误打误撞进入
expressions.definition: to enter a situation awkwardly or by accident
expressions.example: The player seems to bumble into a lively pirate sitcom.

expressions.definition: consistent with a person's established personality
expressions.example: Getting lost remains true to the inexperienced hero's character.

expressions.cn: 满怀热情且天真兴奋的
expressions.definition: very eager, alert, and enthusiastic, often because of inexperience
expressions.example: The young adventurer enters the pirate world wide-eyed and bushy-tailed.

expressions.definition: to use a particular name or description for something
expressions.example: The team initially referred to the hero as Guy.

expressions.definition: to deliberately develop a humorous idea instead of avoiding it
expressions.example: Later writers leaned into the joke by naming his son Boybrush.

expressions.definition: applying to every part or category
expressions.example: The working process was informal across the board.

expressions.definition: to provide the means or opportunity for an action
expressions.example: The chosen name enabled the writers to parody a famous scene.
